subject.title: [Bug 6.1] Silent config auto-patch from memory-core + error-message auto-fix breaks all cron jobs on hosts without Docker

question: Should OpenClaw treat agent-reachable CLI configuration mutation as a prohibited privilege-escalation path and require a single explicit approval/audit boundary for every automated config write?
rationale: The correct repair spans host execution authority, persisted configuration, sandbox posture, and possibly plugin-owned cron behavior; choosing the lasting authorization policy cannot be resolved from the reporter’s logs alone.

options.title: Establish a unified config-write boundary
options.body: Require explicit operator-approved authority and a distinct audit event for all non-interactive configuration writes, then trace and remove any bypasses.

options.title: Limit the immediate mitigation
options.body: Remove actionable sandbox advice from agent-visible errors first while retaining separate follow-up work to identify all config writers.

options.title: Preserve automated writes with explicit policy
options.body: Allow narrowly scoped automated writes only after defining their owner, approval model, audit records, and rollback behavior.

recommendation.title: Establish a unified config-write boundary
recommendation.body: Require explicit operator-approved authority and a distinct audit event for all non-interactive configuration writes, then trace and remove any bypasses.

likelyOwner.reason: Current-main ownership needs history inspection across the sandbox, CLI configuration, and memory/cron paths before routing to a named contributor.
